title: Reflect. Read. Rise for 9/28
author: James Robinson
summary: Robinson pilots a weekly leadership update from Project Reflect and Smithson Craighead Academy, organised under the headings Reflect, Read and Rise. This week the team ran Quarter 1 Teacher Report walkthroughs, using the teacher report card as the main professional development tool. Student interviews, classroom observations and stack audits showed 94 percent engagement schoolwide, a legibility problem in K-2 and sentence-structure work needed in grades 3-5. Students knew more content but missed the main ideas of their units, and retrieval was not automatic in one grade, which he traces partly to the unit unpacking template. His stance is that if leaders did not give the right guidance, leaders must fix it. The next steps are targeted PD, revised Quarter 2 targets and a Know/Say chart added to the unpacking template.
points: The school uses a teacher report card as its main professional development tool, with clear Quarter 1 goals such as full engagement, strong routines and habits like legibility.
Evidence comes from three sources, student interviews, classroom observations and stack audits, which together reveal gaps a single method would miss.
Interviews showed students retaining content but missing unit main ideas, which Robinson attributes to the unpacking template rather than to teachers.
The leadership posture is accountable: if leaders did not give the right guidance, then leaders need to supply it.
The Reflect, Read, Rise cycle closes the loop with targeted PD, revised report-card targets and a Know/Say chart aligned to each unit's main idea.
quotes: Our teacher report card is our main professional development tool. The goals for quarter 1 are for teachers to engage 100% of students at all times, to establish strong systems and routines, to have lessons internalized, and to establish strong student habits
Our stack audits revealed a legibility issue in K-2. This is a problem that has occurred due to past curricula that lacked a direct instruction approach.

In one grade level, retrieval was not as automatic as we’d expect and required more prompts. Additionally, while the students are more knowledgeable overall, they are missing the main ideas of the units, which is likely due to the current unit unpacking template.
If we, as leaders, didn’t provide the right guidance, then we need to do it.
For instance, when the second grade spoke about ancient Greece, we didn’t hear what we wanted to hear in terms of Democracy. Nor did we hear why gods were relevant.
Additionally, we’ll edit targets on the Quarter 2 Teacher Report Card and add a Know/ Say Chart to the unpacking template that’s aligned to the main idea of the units.
